short_header: Passive Background NLP Widgets (Active GenAI Missing)
plain_desc: Everyday apps silently fix mobile typos, filter inbox spam, translate pages, and rank feeds.
keywords_1line: autocorrect, spam filters, Smart Compose, neural machine translation, spellcheck underline, predictive keyboard, sequence tagger, search ranking
encyclopedic_body:
• Extended Summary: Invisible background NLP utilities inside consumer apps automatically correct typos via autocorrect, filter inbox spam, run neural machine translation, and suggest predictive keyboard replies.
• Use Cases & Landmarks: Gmail Smart Compose launch (2018-05, KDD 2019), Google Neural Machine Translate (GNMT, 2016), Grammarly browser typo underlines, iOS QuickType predictions, and automated inbox spam filtering.
• User Actions: Typing normal everyday emails, web search queries, or mobile text messages while clicking single-word red spellcheck underlines or pressing Tab on fixed three-word phrase completions (0% prompting).
• Models & Products: Google GNMT LSTM-Transformer hybrid encoder-decoder, Grammarly GECToR sequence tagger, Gmail Smart Compose language model, iOS QuickType neural LM, and Bayesian/neural spam classifiers.
• Surface & Hardware: Chrome and Safari browser extensions, iOS and Android mobile keyboards, Gmail web client, and background cloud CPU/TPU inference pipelines operating silently at sub-20ms keystroke latency.
• Scope & Evolution: Sits at the zero-study consumer entry point above L2 AutoML/regex rules since active chat did not exist yet; custom tasks escalate down to L2 or L3, while L1 evolves rightward into chatbots.

short_header: No-Code Cloud AutoML Consoles & Regex Rule Crafting
plain_desc: Upload labeled CSV tables to cloud AutoML consoles or build regex rule chatbot trees.
keywords_1line: AutoML tables, regex intent rules, decision-tree bots, entity slots, confidence sliders, confusion matrix, webhook routing, precision-recall
encyclopedic_body:
• Extended Summary: Domain power-users automate ticket routing and FAQ bots without writing Python by uploading labeled CSV datasets to cloud AutoML tables or crafting regex intent rules and entity slot decision trees.
• Use Cases & Landmarks: Google Cloud AutoML Vision/NLP launch (2018-01), AWS Comprehend no-code console, Zendesk and Salesforce regex ticket routing trees, and FAQ decision-tree customer support chatbots.
• User Actions: Cleaning and uploading 500–5,000 labeled CSV rows into cloud consoles, crafting regex lookahead/lookbehind intent patterns, and tuning precision-recall confidence threshold GUI sliders.
• Models & Products: Google Cloud AutoML NLP / Vision / Tables neural architecture search, AWS Comprehend, Microsoft Azure LUIS, Google Dialogflow ES intent-entity trees, and Regex101 interactive debugger.
• Surface & Hardware: Browser-based cloud admin consoles, Excel and Google Sheets CSV tabular editors, Regex101 web sandbox, and JSON webhook integrations backed by managed cloud GPU training pools.
• Scope & Evolution: Gives non-coders custom classification that passive L1 widgets above cannot configure without writing L3 Python TF-IDF scripts below; CSV uploads and regex rules sink rightward into L2 prompting.

short_header: Classical Python NLP & Tabular XGBoost Pipelines

keywords_1line: TF-IDF matrices, gradient-boosted trees, scikit-learn, XGBoost, n-gram tokenization, lemmatization, stratified k-fold CV, ROC-AUC curves
encyclopedic_body:
• Extended Summary: Applied software engineers write Python scripts to transform unstructured text into sparse TF-IDF matrices and train scikit-learn or XGBoost gradient-boosted trees validated via stratified k-fold CV.
• Use Cases & Landmarks: Enterprise customer churn and credit risk scoring, Kaggle tabular and text competitions, spaCy v2 neural dependency/NER pipelines (2017-09), and automated financial document extraction.
• User Actions: Writing Python scripts for TF-IDF sparse matrix vectorization, n-gram tokenization, stop-word pruning, multi-table feature joins, stratified k-fold cross-validation, and grid search tuning.
• Models & Products: scikit-learn (LogisticRegression, RandomForest, SVM), XGBoost (Chen & Guestrin), LightGBM, CatBoost, spaCy (en_core_web_sm transition parser), NLTK, and Gensim Word2Vec/FastText.
• Surface & Hardware: Local Jupyter Notebook, Anaconda Python distribution, Pandas/NumPy/SciPy DataFrames, and multi-core CPU workstations or standard cloud virtual machines without specialized GPU accelerators.
• Scope & Evolution: Replaces rigid GUI templates of L2 AutoML above with custom Python feature engineering while avoiding L4 BERT GPU costs below; basic text classification sinks upward into next-gen L2 prompts.

short_header: Single-GPU Pretrained Encoder Fine-Tuning (BERT / RoBERTa)
plain_desc: Rent single cloud GPUs to fine-tune pretrained BERT and RoBERTa text encoders in PyTorch.
keywords_1line: pretrained encoders, BERT fine-tuning, WordPiece tokens, [CLS] classification head, AdamW warmup, cosine decay, SQuAD extractive QA, NER
encyclopedic_body:

• Use Cases & Landmarks: Google BERT open-source release (2018-10), Grammarly GECToR grammatical error tagger (2020), SQuAD 2.0 extractive question answering, clinical/legal NER, and contract clause extraction.

• Models & Products: Google BERT-base/large (Devlin 2018), Facebook RoBERTa (Liu 2019), DistilBERT, ALBERT, Fast.ai ULMFiT, AllenNLP, and HuggingFace pytorch-pretrained-bert / transformers library.
• Surface & Hardware: PyTorch training scripts in Google Colab Pro or AWS/GCP instances running on a single 16GB NVIDIA V100, Tesla T4, or GTX 1080 Ti GPU monitored via TensorBoard loss curves.
• Scope & Evolution: Captures bidirectional context that bag-of-words L3 classifiers above miss (+15 F1 pts) without managing L5 multi-GPU clusters below; general NLP sinks to L2/L3 prompting while tuning evolves to QLoRA.
